items.headline: Muay Thai fighter, 24, who died after a charity bout donates organs to save four lives
items.summary: Damian Ong, 24, suffered a traumatic brain injury at a charity Muay Thai bout on 12 September and died on 27 September after two weeks in intensive care. His organ donation gave four patients a transplant, including two who had been on dialysis for eight and nine years.

items.headline: SGX to cut board lot sizes, making blue-chip stocks far cheaper to buy from 5 October
items.summary: From 5 October the Singapore Exchange will lower the standard board lot for 11 higher-priced stocks, including DBS, OCBC, and UOB, from 100 shares to 10, and to a single share for stocks trading above S$100.

items.headline: Hair studio caught buying fake reviews says staff acted on their own to earn incentives
items.summary: A Singapore hair studio named in a CCCS case against 45 businesses that bought fake reviews said some staff had procured the reviews independently to earn incentives.

items.headline: Police appeal for information on a 15-year-old girl missing since late September in Pasir Ris
items.summary: Singapore police issued a public appeal for a 15-year-old girl last seen near Pasir Ris Rise at about 6:30am on 24 September.

items.headline: Update: Police detain protesters as the 'Cockroach' movement takes its voter-roll fight to Delhi and Mumbai
items.summary: Security forces bundled demonstrators into buses on 2 October as the Cockroach Janta Party and student groups launched fresh protests in New Delhi and Mumbai, demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign over voter-roll revisions.

items.headline: US says a trade deal with India is not imminent after a Modi-Trump call
items.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an agreement with New Delhi was not close, with India still facing the threat of up to 100 percent US tariffs over its purchases of Russian oil.

items.headline: Jaishankar delivers a blunt critique of the US over terrorism, Pakistan, and trade
items.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar called the US an insensitive partner on India's terrorism concerns, criticised Washington's warming ties with Pakistan, and faulted its self-centred trade policies.

items.headline: Indian stocks slide to their lowest since March as a global bond rout and high oil weigh
items.summary: The NSE Nifty 50 fell about 0.9 percent to its lowest close since 30 March as a worldwide bond sell-off and elevated crude prices drove a risk-off move.

items.headline: Two Iranian men charged over an alleged Yom Kippur attack plot on Manchester's Jewish community
items.summary: UK prosecutors charged two Iranian men with preparing acts of terrorism over an alleged plot targeting Manchester's Jewish community on the eve of Yom Kippur. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the suspects had arrived by small boat.

items.headline: Burnham says a referendum on rejoining the EU is 'possible' in a future manifesto
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham said a vote on rejoining the EU was possible in a future election platform, though not now, arguing the UK must consider its options.

items.headline: UK gilts rebound and the pound firms as the global bond sell-off eases
items.summary: British government bonds recovered on 2 October after the 30-year gilt yield had earlier spiked to about 6.03 percent, its highest since 1998.

items.headline: Pakistani air strikes in Afghanistan kill civilians as border tensions flare
items.summary: Afghanistan's Taliban government said Pakistani air strikes on Kunar and Helmand killed about nine to 10 people, mostly women and children; Islamabad said it hit militant hideouts and killed around 22 TTP and BLA fighters.

items.headline: Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia as fears of a regional war grow
items.summary: Eritrea cut diplomatic relations with Ethiopia after Addis Ababa expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats and moved to shut its embassy in Asmara amid renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia.

items.headline: Avalanche kills at least 15 expedition workers at a Himalayan base camp in Nepal
items.summary: An avalanche buried the base camp of the 7,126-metre Himlung Himal in Nepal's Manang district, killing at least 15 Nepali workers; rescuers recovered eight more bodies on Thursday.

items.headline: US to send a third aircraft carrier toward Iran in its biggest regional buildup since 2003
items.summary: A US official told Al Jazeera the USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group had left San Diego for the Middle East, joining two carriers already deployed against Iran as the conflict entered its eighth month.

items.headline: Amazon unveils the Kindle Click, a $35 page-turning remote, with a redesigned e-reader line
items.summary: Amazon introduced the Kindle Click, a $34.99 Bluetooth remote for hands-free page turning, alongside restyled Kindle, Paperwhite, and Colorsoft readers; the remote works with 2024-or-later Kindles and ships on 28 October.

items.headline: Amazon seeks to move about $8 billion of Nvidia chips off its balance sheet
items.summary: Amazon is exploring a deal to shift roughly $8 billion of top-end Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips into an outside-funded special-purpose vehicle, keeping use of the hardware under an asset-light model, the FT reported.

items.headline: SoftBank completes its final $10 billion payment in a $30 billion OpenAI investment
items.summary: SoftBank said it had paid the last $10 billion tranche of the $30 billion it pledged in OpenAI's latest round, alongside a matching Nvidia payment, taking its total OpenAI investment to about $64.6 billion for a roughly 13 percent stake.

items.headline: OpenAI and Synopsys team up on an AI model built to design computer chips
items.summary: Synopsys struck a multi-year, revenue-sharing deal with OpenAI to build GPT-Synopsys, a model trained to run its chip-design software; Synopsys shares rose as much as 7 percent and it lifted its fiscal-2027 growth forecast to 15 percent.

items.headline: US hiring stalls as the economy adds just 29,000 jobs and unemployment rises to 4.2%
items.summary: The September jobs report showed nonfarm payrolls up only 29,000, far below the roughly 84,000 expected, with unemployment rising to 4.2 percent; traders put about a 77 percent chance the Fed holds rates in October.

items.headline: Stocks rise and the Nasdaq hits a record as Nvidia leads a tech rally
items.summary: US stocks climbed on Friday after the soft jobs data, with the Dow up about 250 points to 51,176 and the Nasdaq Composite closing at a record led by a fresh high in Nvidia.

items.headline: Tesla delivers 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, beating expectations
items.summary: Tesla reported 486,532 deliveries for the third quarter, above analyst estimates of about 461,100 and up from 480,126 in Q2, though down roughly 2 percent from 497,099 a year earlier.

items.headline: Oil slips as the G7 prepares to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude
items.summary: Crude prices edged lower on Friday after the G7 said it would release as much as 100 million barrels of diesel and crude over four months to ease fuel costs, with Brent settling near $102 a barrel.

items.headline: Verstappen edges Russell to top opening practice as F1 returns to Sepang
items.summary: Max Verstappen set the pace in first practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix, held at Malaysia's Sepang circuit for the first time since 2017, lapping 1:37.520 to beat George Russell by nearly four tenths, with Isack Hadjar third.

items.headline: Leclerc tops second practice at Sepang ahead of Hadjar and Norris
items.summary: Charles Leclerc led a tight second practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with a 1:37.528, edging Isack Hadjar and Lando Norris, as Mercedes' George Russell and Kimi Antonelli slipped to seventh and eighth.

items.headline: Djokovic rallies past Bu to reach the China Open quarterfinals and stay 31-0 in Beijing
items.summary: Novak Djokovic came from a set down and took a mid-match medical timeout before beating Bu Yunchaokete 4-6, 7-6(2), 6-2 to reach the Beijing quarterfinals, extending his perfect China Open record to 31-0.

items.headline: Snigur stuns 14th seed Paolini in a Beijing upset as qualifiers advance
items.summary: Ukraine's Snigur fought back to beat 14th seed Jasmine Paolini 3-6, 7-6(5), 6-2 at the China Open, one of several second-round upsets in Beijing that also saw qualifier Polina Kudermetova oust 32nd seed Clara Tauson.

items.headline: Landmark genome study rewrites the bat family tree and traces their origin to Europe
items.summary: An international consortium sequenced 103 bat species covering all 21 families and, with fossils, estimated bats arose about 60 million to 65 million years ago in Europe, resolving long-contested branches of the tree.

items.headline: Google launches four AI chips into orbit to test data centres in space
items.summary: Google's Project Suncatcher put a prototype satellite carrying four of its Tensor Processing Units into low-Earth orbit aboard a SpaceX rideshare on 1 October, running Gemini models in roughly 15-minute sessions.

items.headline: Study finds Earth's whole crust has rolled over at least four times since the dinosaurs
items.summary: A new Science study led by the University of Oslo's Mathew Domeier used ancient sea-level records to show the planet's solid shell has slid around its core (true polar wander) at least four times in 320 million years, still shifting about 10 cm a year.

items.headline: NASA launches three small satellites to test new propulsion and inspect dead spacecraft
items.summary: NASA-supported CubeSats launched on 1 October to demonstrate a low-toxicity dual-mode propulsion system, study ultraviolet light from galactic gas and dust (SPRITE), and trial inspection of up to four defunct satellites.

fun_fact.headline: The largest living organism on Earth is a fungus
fun_fact.body: The largest living organism on Earth is a honey fungus (Armillaria ostoyae) in Oregon's Blue Mountains, spanning about 9.6 sq km and estimated to be up to roughly 8,650 years old.

puzzle.title: Short-Changed
puzzle.body: A man cashes a cheque; the teller swaps the dollars and cents. After spending 5 cents he has exactly twice the cheque's value. Find the cheque.
puzzle.approach: Let the cheque be d dollars and c cents; form one equation and solve for whole numbers.

word_puzzle.title: Parchment Trail
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed. Top P R M; Right A C T; Bottom H E S; Left N D O. Solve in two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Hop side to side; consecutive letters cannot share a side; each word starts on the last word's final letter.

notes: Severe network restrictions this run: BBC, Sky News, The Guardian, Reuters, Al Jazeera (fetch), CNBC/Bloomberg/Nature (fetch), and all India primary outlets (The Hindu, Indian Express, Times of India, Hindustan Times, NDTV, Economic Times) were egress- or crawler-blocked, so items were sourced and cross-corroborated via live web search rather than direct fetch, and link resolution could not be re-verified by fetch. India ran on the fallback tier (Al Jazeera, CNBC, Bloomberg): all six India primary outlets were unreachable; 3+ retry angles were attempted per blocked section. UK News ran on the fallback tier (CNN, CNBC, Bloomberg): BBC, Sky News and The Guardian were unreachable; UK carries 3 items (fewer stories today) rather than padding. Singapore ran chiefly on Mothership (CNA, The Straits Times, SCMP unreachable). Two Tech items (SoftBank-OpenAI, OpenAI-Synopsys) are Reuters wire cited via syndication URLs because reuters.com is crawler-blocked. F1 currency confirmed: the current round (Oct 2-4) is the Bahrain Grand Prix held at Sepang, Malaysia; only Friday practice results (FP1 Verstappen, FP2 Leclerc) were carried as qualifying (Oct 3, 16:00 local) had not yet run and Sunday's race had not occurred. The India-Pakistan Asian Games cricket gold-medal final (Oct 3) was NOT carried: it had not been played at run time, so no result was reported. A Gaza/Hamas peace-plan development was dropped due to unresolved date-conflation risk with October 2025 reporting. No whole-brief hard-stop (31 verified items, well above 8).
